newsitem.title: USA: COMEX June gold falls to new contract low.
newsitem.headline: COMEX June gold falls to new contract low.

text.p: COMEX June gold futures fell to a new contract low of $340.20 an ounce shortly after the opening Tuesday.
Analysts said follow-through selling by commodity funds accelerated on weak U.S. March housing starts data and rumors that the Bundesbank was selling gold.

"Mostly it was carryover selling by funds from Tuesday, after the U.S. March CPI data, but producer hedging is likely also as the fundamentals right now are just an invitation to sell," Refco New York analyst James Steel said.
COMEX June was down $3.40 at $340.50 after the first half hour.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $338.50/$339.00, not far from the three-year low of $336.15 posted Feb 12.

After trading between $348 and $358 in the past month, the latest slippage was led by Australian producer selling Tuesday, combined with the execution of stop orders by funds below $348.00 in the June contract, traders said.
But a less-than-expected rise of 0.1 percent in March U.S. consumer prices added to reasons for disinvestment from gold, analysts said.
Analysts also cited a U.S. March housing starts drop of 6.4 percent which suggests building activity was slightly weaker than expected.
